title: Missing Authorization Check in Poll Voters Endpoint Discloses Voters and Poll Data on Private Topics
analysis:
### Vulnerability Details

#### Source
Untrusted input enters via HTTP GET query parameters `post_id`, `poll_name`, and optional pagination parameters (`limit`, `page`, `option_id`) to the public endpoint `/polls/voters.json`. In `plugins/poll/app/controllers/polls_controller.rb`, the controller specifies:
`before_action :ensure_logged_in, except: %i[voters grouped_poll_results]`
This allows unauthenticated external requests to reach `voters`.

#### Sanitization / Validation Bypass
The method attempts validation with two checks:
1. `raise Discourse::InvalidParameters.new(:post_id) if !Post.where(id: post_id).exists?`
This query merely checks for the existence of a record in the `posts` table. It does not check if the post is deleted (`trashed?`), nor does it check whether the requesting user has permission to see the post (`guardian.can_see_post?(post)`), its topic (`guardian.can_see_topic?(topic)`), or its category.
2. `poll = Poll.find_by(post_id: post_id, name: poll_name)` followed by `raise Discourse::InvalidParameters.new(:poll_name) if !poll&.can_see_voters?(current_user)`
In `Poll#can_see_voters?(user)`, the logic evaluates:
`everyone? && can_see_results?(user)`
`everyone?` is true whenever the poll was created with public visibility (`visibility: "everyone"`). `can_see_results?(user)` evaluates `always? || (on_vote? && (is_me?(user) || has_voted?(user))) || is_closed?`. For default polls where results visibility is `always` (or if the poll is closed), `can_see_results?` evaluates to `true` even when `current_user` is `nil` (anonymous). Neither check verifies whether the topic or post itself is a private message (PM), staff-only topic, or located in a restricted category.

#### Sink
The server passes `poll` directly to `DiscoursePoll::Poll.serialized_voters(poll, opts)` and renders `{ voters: ... }` as JSON, leaking the option digests and user profiles (ID, username, name, avatar template) of all voters.

#### Conceptual Exploit Payload
An unauthenticated attacker sends:
```http
GET /polls/voters.json?post_id=1234&poll_name=poll HTTP/1.1
Host: discourse.example.com
Accept: application/json
```
Where `post_id=1234` is a post in a confidential private message (PM) or restricted category containing a public poll. The server returns HTTP 200 with JSON detailing the poll option IDs and the usernames and profiles of users who voted in that confidential discussion.
snippet:
def voters
    post_id = params.require(:post_id)
    poll_name = params.require(:poll_name)
    opts = params.permit(:limit, :page, :option_id)

    raise Discourse::InvalidParameters.new(:post_id) if !Post.where(id: post_id).exists?

    poll = Poll.find_by(post_id: post_id, name: poll_name)
    raise Discourse::InvalidParameters.new(:poll_name) if !poll&.can_see_voters?(current_user)

    render json: { voters: DiscoursePoll::Poll.serialized_voters(poll, opts) }
  end

title: Authorization Bypass in Onebox Local Topic Resolution Exposes Shared Draft Topic Previews
analysis:
### Vulnerability Details

#### Source
Untrusted input enters via the endpoints `OneboxController#show` (`/onebox`) and `InlineOneboxController#show` (`/inline-onebox`) through request query parameters `url` (or `urls[]`) and `category_id`. Both endpoints pass `params[:category_id].to_i` into options provided to `Oneboxer.preview` and `InlineOneboxer.new`.

#### Sanitization / Validation Bypass
`Oneboxer.local_topic` attempts to validate access to local topics linked via URL:
1. It looks up `current_category = Category.find_by(id: opts[:category_id])` and checks `Guardian.new(current_user).can_see_category?(current_category)`.
2. It finds the target topic linked in the URL: `topic = Topic.find_by(id: route[:id] || route[:topic_id])`.
3. It performs:
```ruby
    if current_category.blank? || current_category.id != topic.category_id
      return unless Guardian.new.can_see_topic?(topic)
    end
```
This validation is fundamentally flawed:
- An attacker can specify `category_id` equal to `topic.category_id` (a category the user can access, such as any public category).
- When `current_category.id == topic.category_id`, the check `Guardian.new.can_see_topic?(topic)` is entirely bypassed.
- Discourse supports "Shared Drafts" (`shared_draft: true`), which are drafts stored in categories awaiting publication. `TopicGuardian#can_see_topic?` restricts shared drafts:
`return false if topic.shared_draft && !can_see_shared_draft?`
Because `Oneboxer.local_topic` never checks `Guardian.new(current_user).can_see_topic?(topic)` when `current_category.id == topic.category_id`, regular users who lack permission to view shared drafts completely bypass the topic visibility check.
- Additionally, even when `current_category.id != topic.category_id`, the code falls back to `Guardian.new.can_see_topic?(topic)`, testing against an anonymous Guardian rather than `current_user`'s Guardian permissions.

#### Sink
The unauthorized `topic` is returned. In `Oneboxer.local_topic_html`, its first post is read and excerpted (`post.excerpt(SiteSetting.post_onebox_maxlength)`), formatted into a Mustache template with its title, author, and content quote, and returned in the HTTP response. In `InlineOneboxController`, the topic title is returned in JSON.

#### Conceptual Exploit Payload
A normal authenticated user without staff/shared-draft permissions requests:
```http
GET /onebox?url=https://discourse.example.com/t/topic-slug/567&category_id=1 HTTP/1.1
Host: discourse.example.com
Cookie: _forum_session=...
```
Where topic `567` is an unpublished shared draft residing in public category `1`. Because `category_id=1` matches `topic.category_id`, the topic-level visibility check is bypassed. The server returns HTTP 200 with the rendered HTML onebox preview containing the secret topic title, author information, and post content excerpt.
